### 1. Keep route ownership stable; move HTML construction into templates

**Claim**: In Crow-style apps, routes should remain the URL/method boundary, while server-rendered HTML should be produced by loading a Mustache template, building a `crow::mustache::context`, and returning `page.render(ctx)`.

**Evidence** ([Crow templating docs](https://github.com/CrowCpp/Crow/blob/326e96b844ae79c0845d11b124818985ee860848/docs/guides/templating.md#L34-L55)):

```cpp
auto page = crow::mustache::load("path/to/template.html");
crow::mustache::context ctx;
ctx["key"] = value;
return page.render(ctx);
```

**Explanation**: For BankSystem, this supports moving route-rendered HTML strings into root templates and fragment templates without changing route URLs or handler responsibilities. Routes can keep assembling domain data, but the HTML structure should live in templates.

---

### 2. Use root templates for full pages and fragment templates for reusable sections

**Claim**: Crow Mustache supports partial templates, so a root page can include smaller reusable fragments such as nav bars, account tables, alert banners, transaction rows, or forms.

**Evidence** ([Crow mustache unit test](https://github.com/CrowCpp/Crow/blob/326e96b844ae79c0845d11b124818985ee860848/tests/unit_tests/test_mustache.cpp#L130-L139)):

```cpp
TEST_CASE("template_partial", "[mustache]") 
{
    mustache::set_base(".");
    std::ofstream("partial.mustache") << "tomatoes";
    std::ofstream("main.mustache") << R"---(killer {{> partial.mustache}})---";
    auto main_template = mustache::load("main.mustache");
    mustache::context ctx;
    auto result = main_template.render_string(ctx);
    CHECK(result == "killer tomatoes");
```

**Explanation**: A BankSystem template plan can use root templates like `dashboard.html`, `accounts.html`, `transactions.html`, and fragments like `fragments/account_row.html`, `fragments/flash.html`, or `fragments/nav.html`. The route still renders the root template; the root template pulls in fragments.

### 3. Prefer `load()` over unsafe template loading

**Claim**: Template paths loaded by `crow::mustache::load()` are sanitized before compilation; unsafe loading bypasses that sanitizer and is explicitly warned against.

**Evidence** ([Crow source](https://github.com/CrowCpp/Crow/blob/326e96b844ae79c0845d11b124818985ee860848/include/crow/mustache.h#L853-L874)):

```cpp
inline template_t load(const std::string& filename)
{
    std::string filename_sanitized(filename);
    utility::sanitize_filename(filename_sanitized);
    return compile(detail::get_loader_ref()(filename_sanitized));
}

inline template_t load_unsafe(const std::string& filename)
{
    return compile(detail::get_loader_ref()(filename));
}
```

**Explanation**: For a banking app, avoid route parameters directly selecting arbitrary template files. Hard-code template names in handlers and pass only data through `ctx`.
